title: Article 226A — Constitutional validity of Central laws not to be considered under Article 226 (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 226A barred High Courts from considering the constitutional validity of Central laws in Article 226 proceedings. It was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13 April 1978), restoring High Court competence.
content.glance: Art 226A omitted by 43rd Amendment 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). HC bar on Central-law validity removed.
content.study:
Article 226A was an Emergency-era restriction channeling Central-law validity challenges away from High Courts.

Omission: Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978).

Living frame: High Courts may examine the validity of Central laws in appropriate Article 226 proceedings subject to living doctrine and practice.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 226A as a current bar.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted by the 42nd Amendment; omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978).

misconceptions.trap: High Courts still cannot decide the constitutional validity of Central laws because of Article 226A.
misconceptions.correction: Article 226A was omitted by the 43rd Amendment, 1977. It is not living law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 226A?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 226A was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). High Courts are not barred by that omitted article from considering Central-law validity under Article 226.

examTips: Pair with Art 131A and other 43rd Amendment judicial restorations.
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 43rd Amendment omission. Case-law gate open.

notes: Omission by 43rd Amendment w.e.f. 13-4-1978. No invented holdings.
